listed here. This is what stops parallel agents inventing plausible-but-broken links.
2. REVERSE INDEX — "sources" maps source files back to the concepts that describe them,
which is how drift detection knows what a given code change made stale.
3. DRIFT BASELINE — "baseline_sha" is the commit the whole vault was last verified against.

concepts.description: Session-close checklist that commits outstanding work, updates the Linear ticket and preserves context before a context switch.
concepts.notes: invoked as /end-work (Claude) or /workflow:end-work (Gemini) | no args | 6 ordered steps: (1) git status + git log origin/dev..HEAD --oneline to classify Complete / In Progress / Blocked (2) git add . && git commit -m 'type(scope): description [{{TICKET_PREFIX}}-XXX]' then re-check git status (3) doc checklist: inline comments, README, CLAUDE.md/CONTRIBUTING.md, ticket status (4) Linear write via mcp__{{MCP_LINEAR_SERVER}}__update_issue and mcp__{{MCP_LINEAR_SERVER}}__create_comment, branching on the 3 statuses (5) write a Session Context markdown block if stopping mid-work (6) branch decision: git push origin {branch-name}, or keep local, or WIP PR | WRITE COMMAND: this is one of the few commands that stages and commits with 'git add .' — it commits everything in the tree, not a scoped set | notes GitHub-Linear integration auto-syncs tickets referenced in commit messages to Done on PR merge; child stories not referenced must be closed manually | references /pre-pr as the follow-on | preconditions: git repo, origin/dev, Linear MCP | BRANCH DRIFT: Claude uses origin/dev; Gemini toml uses origin/main | PARITY GAP: Gemini has no Linear MCP calls (step 4 is prose only) and drops the 'If Experimental' WIP-PR branch of step 6 | PARITY GAP: Gemini 'suggests' committing rather than running git add/commit itself

concepts.title: /local-deploy
concepts.description: Deploys the latest registry Docker image to the local Docker daemon in dev or staging mode, optionally triggering a CI build first.
concepts.notes: invoked as /local-deploy [--staging] [--rebuild] (Claude) or /local:deploy (Gemini) | 7 ordered steps: (1) parse flags into MODE and REBUILD shell vars (2) pre-deploy status: docker ps on {{PROJECT_NAME}}-staging-app and {{PROJECT_NAME}}-dev-app, docker inspect for org.opencontainers.image.revision, git log origin/dev -1 (3) if --rebuild: gh workflow run 'Build and Push Dev Docker Image' --ref dev, sleep 10, gh run list to get databaseId, poll gh run view every 30s until completed, exit 1 on non-success conclusion (4) deploy: staging path runs ./scripts/dev-docker.sh deploy; dev path runs ./scripts/dev-docker.sh pull then ./scripts/dev-docker.sh restart (5) verify via docker ps and curl localhost:3000 or :3001 /api/health (6) docker logs --tail 50 (7) print deployment report | calls the helper script ./scripts/dev-docker.sh with subcommands deploy, pull, restart, stop, stop-staging, start, logs | port map: dev app 3000 / postgres 5432 / redis 6379; staging app 3001 / postgres 5433 / redis 6380 | documented failure modes: workflow not found (gh workflow list), build fails (gh run view --log), image pull fails (df -h, docker login ghcr.io, docker system prune -a), port conflicts (lsof, stop both stacks, systemctl restart docker), health check fails | rollback offer references /local-rollback which the body itself annotates as '(when available)' | DOC DRIFT: the Deployment Modes table documents a --both flag but the step-1 argument parser only branches on --staging and --rebuild, so --both is never parsed | DOC DRIFT: Related Commands lists /local-health, /local-logs, /local-restart, /local-rollback — none of these exist under .claude/commands/ | DOC DRIFT: Gemini toml targets origin/main and workflow name 'Build and Push Docker Image' where Claude targets origin/dev and 'Build and Push Dev Docker Image' | PARITY GAP: Gemini toml drops the --both mode, the port allocation tables, the mode-switching section and the report template

concepts.title: /local-sync
concepts.description: Post-pull local environment sync: branch cleanup, git pull, change-gated yarn install and Prisma generate, optional CI validation.
concepts.notes: invoked as /local-sync (Claude) or /local:sync (Gemini) | no args | 9 ordered steps: (1) git branch --show-current, stash if dirty, git checkout dev (2) git pull origin dev with stash/pop fallback (3) cleanup: git branch --merged dev, git branch -d, git fetch --prune origin, git for-each-ref to list stale branches (4) change detection: DEPS_CHANGED=git diff HEAD@{1} HEAD -- package.json yarn.lock; SCHEMA_CHANGED=git diff HEAD@{1} HEAD -- prisma/schema.prisma prisma/migrations/ (5) yarn install only if DEPS_CHANGED non-empty (6) npx prisma generate + npx prisma migrate status only if SCHEMA_CHANGED non-empty (7) yarn ci:validate only on explicit user opt-in (default is skip) (8) docker ps --filter name={{PROJECT_NAME}} (9) print sync report | ci:validate is documented as type-check + lint + test:unit | gating uses HEAD@{1} reflog, so the detection is wrong if the pull was a no-op or if the reflog was rewritten — behavior in that case UNKNOWN | documented failure modes: merge conflict (manual resolve, re-run), yarn install failure (yarn cache clean, rm -rf node_modules, reinstall), prisma generate failure (npx prisma validate, npx prisma generate --force), ci:validate failure (per-tool drill-down), pending migrations (offers migrate deploy or migrate dev) | suggests ./scripts/dev-docker.sh start or docker-compose up -d if services are down | BRANCH DRIFT: Claude checks out and pulls dev; Gemini toml checks out and pulls main and merges against main | PARITY GAP: Gemini drops the stale-branch listing (git for-each-ref), the SCHEMA_CHANGED detection variable (it only diffs package.json/yarn.lock), and the full report template | PARITY GAP: Gemini runs yarn install / prisma generate / ci:validate through !{...} with '|| echo' fallbacks, so a failure is swallowed rather than surfaced | DANGLING REFS: the Related Commands section points at /local-health, /local-restart and /local-logs; none of these exist as files in .claude/commands/ (verified by listing the directory), and unlike local-deploy.md this file does not hedge them with '(when available)'

concepts.title: /media:analyze-audio

concepts.notes: invoked as /media:analyze-audio <path> [--summary|--detailed|--json] | GEMINI-ONLY: no .claude/commands counterpart exists, so this capability has zero Claude parity | target passed via {{args}} | 4 ordered steps: (1) !{file {{args}} || echo "File not found"} to verify existence and format (2) classify into Speech / Music / Ambient / Mixed (3) branch analysis by type — speech gets language+dialect, pace in WPM, emotional tone, clarity; music gets genre, tempo, instrumentation, mood/energy; ambient/mixed gets source identification, layering, dominant vs background (4) emit the Audio Analysis Report template with File Info, Content Type, Mood & Tone, a timestamped Key Segments table, and Technical Quality (clarity, background noise, dynamic range, overall) | accepted formats: MP3, WAV, AIFF, AAC, OGG, FLAC (6) | output modes: --summary (default), --detailed, --json | stated preconditions: Gemini 3+ required for audio processing | the actual analysis is model multimodal inference, not a shell tool — the only shell call is `file` | failure handling: the single shell call has an '|| echo "File not found"' fallback; no other failure path is defined | PRIVACY: the file states audio contents are sent to the Gemini API for analysis | duration estimates are explicitly approximate | no file size limit is stated here, unlike the video and dialogue commands which cap at 100MB — UNKNOWN whether the same cap applies to this command

concepts.title: /media:analyze-video
concepts.description: Gemini-only command that breaks a video into scenes and reports setting, subjects, actions, dialogue and visual style per scene.
concepts.notes: invoked as /media:analyze-video <path> [--summary|--detailed|--json|--timestamps] | GEMINI-ONLY: no .claude/commands counterpart | target via {{args}} | 4 ordered steps: (1) !{file {{args}} || echo "File not found"} (2) scene analysis through multimodal input — identify scenes and transitions, describe visuals, detect objects/people/actions/settings, note camera movement and composition, transcribe dialogue and on-screen text (3) per scene capture Setting, Subjects, Actions, Dialogue, Visual Style (4) emit the Video Analysis Report with File Info, per-scene blocks carrying start-end timestamps and a Transition field, a Summary narrative arc, and Visual Style Notes (dominant colors, camera work, editing pace) | accepted formats: MP4, MOV, AVI, MKV, WEBM (5) | output modes: --summary (default), --detailed, --json, --timestamps | HARD LIMIT: video files up to 100MB supported | stated preconditions: Gemini 3+ required for video processing | longer videos are explicitly sampled at key intervals rather than analysed exhaustively, so scene lists for long inputs are lossy by design | the audio track is analysed alongside the visual content, which overlaps this command with /media:video-to-script and /media:scene-detect — the three read the same input and differ only in output shape | only shell call is `file`; all analysis is model inference | PRIVACY: video contents are sent to the Gemini API | UNKNOWN: what happens when the input exceeds 100MB — no error path is defined in source

concepts.title: /media:extract-dialogue
concepts.description: Gemini-only command that transcribes audio with speaker diarization, emitting screenplay, JSON or plain labeled transcript.
concepts.notes: invoked as /media:extract-dialogue <path> [--screenplay|--json|--transcript] [--speakers N] | GEMINI-ONLY: no .claude/commands counterpart | target via {{args}} | 4 ordered steps: (1) !{file {{args}} || echo "File not found"} (2) speaker identification — estimate unique speaker count, assign consistent Speaker N labels, note pitch/pace/accent for differentiation, flag overlapping speech (3) transcribe with speaker attribution, per-turn timestamps, preserved pauses and interruptions, and non-verbal sounds (laughter, applause, silence) (4) format into one of three shapes | accepted formats: MP3, WAV, AIFF, AAC, OGG, FLAC (6) | output modes: --screenplay (default), --json (speakers array plus dialogue array of {speaker,start,end,text}), --transcript (Speaker N [HH:MM:SS]: text) | --speakers N is a hint for expected speaker count, not a constraint | HARD LIMIT: audio files up to 100MB | stated preconditions: Gemini 3+ required for audio processing | accuracy caveats stated in source: speaker identification is approximate and voice-characteristic based, improves with distinct voices and minimal crosstalk, and overlapping segments are flagged but have reduced accuracy | overlaps /media:transcribe-audio, which also emits speaker labels when multiple speakers are detected — the distinction is that diarization is this command's primary output rather than a side effect | only shell call is `file`; diarization is model inference with no external ASR or diarization library | PRIVACY: audio contents are sent to the Gemini API

concepts.title: /media:extract-frames

concepts.notes: invoked as /media:extract-frames <path> [--storyboard|--detailed|--json] [--max N] | GEMINI-ONLY: no .claude/commands counterpart | target via {{args}} | 4 ordered steps: (1) !{file {{args}} || echo "File not found"} (2) identify key frames on five signals — scene changes, significant moments (key actions/reactions/events), composition shifts, text appearances (title cards, lower thirds, captions), subject changes (3) per frame emit precise timestamp, detailed visual description, subjects and objects, composition/framing notes, narrative relevance (4) render either the markdown Key Frame Report or the Storyboard table (# / Timestamp / Visual / Action / Audio-Dialogue) | accepted formats: MP4, MOV, AVI, MKV, WEBM (5) | output modes: --storyboard (default), --detailed, --json, --max N (default 20 key frames) | HARD LIMIT: video files up to 100MB | stated preconditions: Gemini 3+ required for video processing | NAMING DRIFT: the command is named extract-frames but it extracts no image files to disk — it produces textual descriptions of frames only; no ffmpeg, no image write, no output path is involved anywhere in the source | frame selection is explicitly based on visual significance rather than fixed intervals, and the source states the frame count varies by content complexity, so results are not reproducible across runs | stated purpose: storyboard generation and edit decision support | only shell call is `file`; all frame identification is model inference | PRIVACY: video contents are sent to the Gemini API

concepts.title: /media:extract-pdf

concepts.notes: invoked as /media:extract-pdf <path-or-directory> [--json|--csv|--markdown|--text] | GEMINI-ONLY: no .claude/commands counterpart | target via {{args}} | 4 ordered steps: (1) !{ls -la {{args}} || echo "File not found"} — note this command uses ls -la for detection where the audio and video media commands use `file` (2) read and analyse structure: identify document type (invoice, form, report, contract), detect tables/forms/structured content, extract text with section awareness (3) extract per type — invoices/receipts to a JSON shape with vendor, invoice_number, date, items[{description,quantity,price}], subtotal, tax, total; tables to CSV; forms to a flat JSON field map (4) emit in the requested format | declared capabilities: text extraction with formatting preservation, table detection with CSV/JSON export, form field extraction, invoice/receipt parsing, multi-page processing | batch mode: passing a directory processes all PDFs in it and generates combined output — the combining rule for heterogeneous document types is not specified | HARD LIMIT: PDFs up to 100MB (stated as Gemini 3) | accuracy caveats stated in source: complex layouts may require multiple passes, handwritten OCR quality varies, scanned documents need good image quality | the only shell call is ls -la; all extraction is model inference — no pdftotext, no OCR library, no parsing dependency | DOC DRIFT: unlike every other media command this file carries no Privacy note, yet document contents are necessarily sent to the Gemini API by the same mechanism — the omission is inconsistent with the other ten | UNKNOWN: whether extracted output is written to disk or only returned in-conversation — no output path is defined

concepts.title: /media:organize-files
concepts.description: Gemini-only command that renames and refiles a directory by analysing file contents rather than extensions, behind a dry-run plan.
concepts.notes: invoked as /media:organize-files <directory> [--dry-run|--images-only|--documents-only|--date-prefix|--no-subfolders|--interactive] | GEMINI-ONLY: no .claude/commands counterpart | target via {{args}} | THE ONLY DESTRUCTIVE MEDIA COMMAND: it renames and moves files on disk; the other ten are read-and-describe | 5 ordered steps: (1) !{find {{args}} -type f -not -path "*/.*" | head -50} and !{find ... | wc -l} for a count (2) categorise by type via a 5-row table — Images (png,jpg,gif,webp) visual analysis, Documents (pdf,doc,docx) text extraction, Audio (mp3,wav,aac) metadata/transcription, Code (js,ts,py) purpose detection, Data (json,csv,xml) schema analysis (3) content-based routing: screenshots/, photos/people/, photos/products/, diagrams/, icons/, documents/invoices|contracts|reports|receipts/, tests/, utils/ (4) smart renaming using EXIF date plus content, e.g. IMG_1234.jpg -> 2025-01-14_vacation_beach_sunset.jpg (5) present the Organization Plan (Will Create Folders / Will Rename / Will Move tables) and prompt 'Proceed? (y/n)' | four stated safety features: dry-run first always shows the plan before execution, backup is recommended before bulk operations, an undo script is generated to reverse changes, hidden/system files are skipped (enforced by -not -path "*/.*") | HARD LIMIT: the scan is capped at head -50, so directories larger than 50 files are silently truncated while the wc -l count reports the true total — the plan will therefore under-report on large directories | DOC DRIFT: 'Dry-run first: Always shows plan before execution' is listed as a safety feature, but --dry-run is also listed as an opt-in flag; whether the plan gate is unconditional or flag-gated is contradictory in source | DOC DRIFT: the Notes claim an option to copy instead of move ('Preserve originals'), but no such flag appears in the Options list | UNKNOWN: where the undo script is written and in what language — the source names it but defines neither path nor format | duplicate detection is stated as content hash plus visual similarity, with no threshold given

concepts.title: /media:scene-detect
concepts.description: Gemini-only command that detects and classifies video scene boundaries, emitting a scene table or a CMX 3600 EDL.
concepts.notes: invoked as /media:scene-detect <path> [--table|--edl|--json|--timestamps] | GEMINI-ONLY: no .claude/commands counterpart | target via {{args}} | 4 ordered steps: (1) !{file {{args}} || echo "File not found"} (2) scan for boundaries — significant frame-to-frame visual change, color palette / composition / content shifts, hard cuts and gradual transitions, audio changes coinciding with visual ones (3) classify each transition into 6 named types: Cut, Fade In, Fade Out, Dissolve, Wipe, Jump Cut (4) emit the scene list | accepted formats: MP4, MOV, AVI, MKV, WEBM (5) | output modes: --table (default markdown table with Scene, Start, End, Duration, Transition In, Description), --edl (CMX 3600 Edit Decision List, stated as following the standard for NLE compatibility), --json, --timestamps | report also carries Average Scene Length and a Transition Summary tallying Cuts / Fades / Dissolves / Other | HARD LIMIT: video files up to 100MB | stated preconditions: Gemini 3+ required for video processing | stated purpose: video editing workflows and content indexing | accuracy caveats in source: transition classification is approximate and visual-analysis based; very fast-paced content produces a high scene count | overlaps /media:analyze-video, which also identifies scenes and transitions — the difference is that this command's output is boundary-and-transition metadata (and machine-readable EDL) rather than per-scene narrative description | only shell call is `file`; boundary detection is model inference with no ffmpeg or PySceneDetect dependency | PRIVACY: video contents are sent to the Gemini API

concepts.title: /media:sketch-to-code

review accessibility and responsiveness; add error handling and validation | DOC DRIFT: this file carries no Privacy note despite sending image contents to the Gemini API, unlike the audio and video media commands | UNKNOWN: the exact write path and overwrite behavior when a component of the same name already exists — step 4 resolves a directory but defines no filename collision rule

concepts.title: /media:transcribe-audio
concepts.description: Gemini-only command that transcribes audio to timestamped text, SRT, WebVTT or JSON with automatic language detection.
concepts.notes: invoked as /media:transcribe-audio <path> [--text|--srt|--vtt|--json] | GEMINI-ONLY: no .claude/commands counterpart | target via {{args}} | 3 ordered steps: (1) !{file {{args}} || echo "File not found"} (2) transcribe through multimodal input — automatic language detection (or a specified language), word-level timestamps, speaker labels when multiple speakers are present, low-confidence segments flagged for review (3) format output | accepted formats: MP3, WAV, AIFF, AAC, OGG, FLAC (6) | output modes: --text (default, [HH:MM:SS] prefixed lines), --srt (numbered cues with comma-millisecond timecodes), --vtt (WEBVTT header, dot-millisecond timecodes), --json (segments array of {start,end,text,speaker} as float seconds) | HARD LIMIT: audio files up to 100MB | stated preconditions: Gemini 3+ required for audio processing | accuracy caveats: best results with clear audio and minimal background noise | DOC DRIFT: step 2 promises word-level timestamps but every output example — text, SRT, VTT and JSON — is segment-level or utterance-level; no output mode in this file can express a per-word timestamp | overlaps /media:extract-dialogue: both transcribe the same six audio formats and both attach speaker labels, but this command treats diarization as incidental ('when multiple speakers are detected') while extract-dialogue makes it the primary product and adds a --speakers hint | the source states a language may be 'specified' but defines no flag for doing so — UNKNOWN how a language is passed | only shell call is `file`; transcription is model inference with no external ASR dependency | PRIVACY: audio contents are sent to the Gemini API

concepts.title: /media:video-to-script
concepts.description: Gemini-only command that fuses video transcription and visual analysis into a standard screenplay, narrative or shot list.
concepts.notes: invoked as /media:video-to-script <path> [--screenplay|--narrative|--shot-list|--json] | GEMINI-ONLY: no .claude/commands counterpart | target via {{args}} | 4 ordered steps: (1) !{file {{args}} || echo "File not found"} (2) transcribe the audio track — all dialogue with speaker attribution, sound effects and ambient audio, music cues and transitions, non-verbal vocalizations (3) analyse the visual track in parallel — interior/exterior scene locations, character actions and movements, camera angles and transitions, on-screen text and graphics (4) merge both tracks into screenplay format with FADE IN/OUT, INT./EXT. scene headings, action paragraphs, centred character cues and dialogue, and CUT TO / CLOSE-UP directions | accepted formats: MP4, MOV, AVI, MKV, WEBM (5) | output modes: --screenplay (default), --narrative (prose), --shot-list (technical shots), --json (structured scene data) | HARD LIMIT: video files up to 100MB | stated preconditions: Gemini 3+ required for video processing | accuracy caveats stated in source: speaker names default to 'Speaker N' unless identifiable, INT/EXT scene headings are inferred from visual context rather than known, and camera direction notes are approximate | this is the fusion command of the video trio — /media:analyze-video describes scenes, /media:scene-detect emits boundaries and EDL, and this one merges audio and visual into a formatted script; all three accept the same 5 formats and the same 100MB cap and differ only in output shape | only shell call is `file`; the merge is model inference with no NLE or subtitle tooling involved | PRIVACY: video contents are sent to the Gemini API

concepts.title: /pre-pr

concepts.title: /quick-fix
concepts.description: Fast-track bug-fix workflow with reduced validation, a minimal PR template and explicit scope limits.
concepts.notes: invoked as /quick-fix [{{TICKET_PREFIX}}-number] (Claude, argument-hint declared) or /workflow:quick-fix (Gemini, {{args}}) | 5 ordered steps: (1) fetch ticket via mcp__{{MCP_LINEAR_SERVER}}__get_issue $1, verify it is a bug, git checkout -b {{TICKET_PREFIX}}-$1-fix-{description}; if no arg, ask for the number (2) guided minimal edit then git add . && git commit -m 'fix(scope): resolve {issue} [{{TICKET_PREFIX}}-XXX]' (3) fast validation: yarn type-check, yarn lint, yarn test:unit only (4) git fetch origin && git rebase origin/dev, git push --force-with-lease, create PR from the abbreviated template (5) notify reviewers / Linear / Slack if urgent | explicit scope gate: allowed for critical blocking bugs under 50 lines with no architecture change and adequate existing coverage; forbidden for new features, large refactors, breaking changes, dependency upgrades | explicitly skipped when time-critical: integration tests, E2E tests, build verification | non-negotiable safety checks retained: SAFe commit format, branch naming, Linear reference, type-check + ESLint | post-merge follow-ups: full test suite, docs, prod verification, close ticket | BRANCH DRIFT: Claude rebases onto origin/dev; Gemini toml rebases onto origin/main | PARITY GAP: Gemini has no Linear MCP call — step 1 says 'verify it is a bug fix via Linear' as prose | PARITY GAP: Gemini's !{...} wrappers append '|| echo ... completed' to type-check, lint and test:unit, so the 'essential validations pass' success criterion cannot actually fail the run | branch name pattern uses $1 raw, so passing a full ticket id rather than a bare number yields a doubled prefix — not guarded in source

concepts.title: /release
concepts.description: Six-phase version release: validate, merge PRs, bump version, tag and publish a GitHub Release, sync branches, clean up.
concepts.notes: invoked as /release <version> e.g. v2.7.0 (Claude argument-hint) or /workflow:release (Gemini) | if no version given, derives from git tag -l 'v*' | sort -V | tail -1 and bumps minor or asks | 6 phases, no phase may be skipped | Phase 1: git status clean + git branch --show-current == {{MAIN_BRANCH}} + git fetch + git log origin/{{MAIN_BRANCH}}..HEAD empty (BLOCKER); gh pr list --state open; gh pr view --json mergeStateStatus,statusCheckRollup per PR (BLOCKER on failing checks) | Phase 2: gh pr merge <N> --squash --subject 'type(scope): description [{{TICKET_PREFIX}}-XXX]' in dependency order, rebase dependent PRs with --force-with-lease, wait for CI between merges, git pull after | Phase 3: grep -rn 'v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' README.md CLAUDE.md CONTRIBUTING.md excluding node_modules/releases/whitepapers; update only active refs not changelogs or KT docs; git add -A && git commit 'chore(release): bump version references to <VERSION>'; git push | Phase 4: git log $LAST_TAG..HEAD grouped into feat/fix/docs/chore; git tag -a <VERSION>; git push origin <VERSION>; gh release create with heredoc notes | Phase 5: git push origin {{MAIN_BRANCH}}:<SECONDARY_BRANCH>; verify both log directions empty; gh api repos/{{GITHUB_ORG}}/{{GITHUB_REPO}}/tags | Phase 6: gh api branches list, gh api -X DELETE .../git/refs/heads/<BRANCH>, git branch --merged | xargs -r git branch -d, git fetch --prune, git gc --prune=now, then a 5-part final verification echo block | DESTRUCTIVE: phase 6 deletes remote refs via gh api -X DELETE and runs git gc --prune=now with no confirmation gate in the source | the version-bump commit template hardcodes 'Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6' | placeholders: {{MAIN_BRANCH}}, {{TICKET_PREFIX}}, {{GITHUB_ORG}}, {{GITHUB_REPO}} | PARITY GAP: Gemini toml is a prose summary of all 6 phases with only one executable !{...} (the git tag list) — no gh commands, no grep, no cleanup commands are actually issued | PARITY GAP: Gemini retains {{MAIN_BRANCH}}/{{TICKET_PREFIX}} placeholders in double-brace form, unlike every other Gemini toml which uses single-brace {PLACEHOLDER}

concepts.title: /remote-deploy

concepts.title: /remote-health
concepts.description: Eight-step remote health dashboard over SSH covering containers, resources, HTTP health, Postgres, Redis, errors and version.
concepts.notes: invoked as /remote-health (Claude) or /remote:health (Gemini) | no args | 8 ordered steps, all read-only: (1) ssh docker ps --filter name={{PROJECT}} and docker inspect --format State.Health.Status (2) ssh docker stats --no-stream, df -h /, docker system df (3) curl -s -w http_code/time_total against http://{{REMOTE_HOST}}:{{APP_PORT}}/api/health (4) ssh docker exec {{DB_CONTAINER}} pg_isready -U {{DB_USER}} (5) ssh docker exec {{REDIS_CONTAINER}} redis-cli ping, expect PONG (6) ssh docker logs --since 5m | grep -i 'error|fatal|exception' | tail -10 (7) ssh docker inspect | grep org.opencontainers.image.revision (8) render dashboard | health score is a 6-criterion additive rubric summing to 100: containers running +30, health checks passing +20, resource usage <80% +15, no recent errors +15, response time <500ms +10, database/Redis responding +10 | score bands: 90-100 Excellent, 70-89 Good, 50-69 Degraded, 0-49 Critical | critical alerts: container stopped, health endpoint down, DB unreachable, disk >90% | warning alerts: response >1s, memory >80%, error spike in last 5m | canonical target of the deprecated /dev-health alias | placeholder key names only: {{SSH_KEY_PATH}}, {{REMOTE_USER}}, {{REMOTE_HOST}}, {{PROJECT}}, {{CONTAINER_NAME}}, {{APP_PORT}}, {{DB_CONTAINER}}, {{DB_USER}}, {{REDIS_CONTAINER}} | PARITY GAP: Gemini toml omits the docker system df call from step 2 and omits the Alert Conditions section entirely, but keeps the identical scoring rubric | PARITY GAP: Gemini uses grep -iE 'error|fatal|exception' where Claude uses grep -i 'error\|fatal\|exception'

concepts.title: /remote-logs
concepts.description: Fetches, filters and analyses remote container logs over SSH with tail, follow and search modes across dev and staging stacks.
concepts.notes: invoked as /remote-logs [--follow] [--tail N] (Claude argument-hint) or /remote:logs {{args}} (Gemini) | 6 ordered steps: (1) mode selection — --follow/-f streams, --tail N limits, no args defaults to 100 lines (2) ssh 'cd {{PROJECT_PATH}} && ./scripts/dev-docker.sh logs --tail 100' for all services, or ssh 'docker logs <container> --tail 100' per service (3) pattern filtering for ERROR/FATAL/Exception/stack traces, WARN/deprecated, and success markers started/listening/ready/connected/successful (4) render per-container analysis block (5) follow mode re-invokes ./scripts/dev-docker.sh logs --follow (6) offer grep search over docker logs | read-only | calls helper ./scripts/dev-docker.sh subcommand logs | addresses six containers across two stacks: {{APP_CONTAINER_DEV}}/{{APP_CONTAINER_STAGING}}, {{DB_CONTAINER_DEV}}/{{DB_CONTAINER_STAGING}}, {{REDIS_CONTAINER_DEV}}/{{REDIS_CONTAINER_STAGING}} | service-name aliases map app|next, postgres|db, redis to the dev or staging container | output modes: Compact (default, filtered), Full (raw), Service-Specific | failure modes: SSH failure (ping {{REMOTE_HOST}}, tailscale status, manual ssh command), container not found (route to /remote-health then /remote-deploy), permission denied (verify docker group, offer sudo) | canonical target of the deprecated /dev-logs alias | DOC DRIFT: step 2's all-services command hardcodes --tail 100 and never substitutes the parsed N from --tail N, so /remote-logs --tail 500 still issues --tail 100 to the helper script | PARITY GAP: Gemini collapses the six dev/staging containers into three generic {APP_CONTAINER}/{DB_CONTAINER}/{REDIS_CONTAINER} and drops the Output Options and service-alias mapping sections

concepts.title: /remote-rollback
concepts.description: Rolls the remote environment back to a prior image by backing up compose, sed-pinning the tag, restarting and verifying health.
concepts.notes: invoked as /remote-rollback [commit-sha] (Claude argument-hint) or /remote:rollback {{args}} (Gemini) | 10 ordered steps: (1) ssh docker inspect for current revision with staging-then-dev fallback via ||, curl health (2) ssh docker images {{REGISTRY}}/{{IMAGE_NAME}} + git log origin/{{MAIN_BRANCH}} -10 --oneline (3) target selection: arg used directly, else show last 5 images and ask for confirmation; default is the image before current (4) ssh docker pull {{REGISTRY}}/{{IMAGE_NAME}}:{{TAG_PREFIX}}-{target-sha}; falls back to local cached image if pruned from registry (5) ssh cp {{COMPOSE_FILE}} {{COMPOSE_FILE}}.backup.$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S) then ssh sed -i to rewrite ':latest' to the pinned tag (6) ssh '{{DOCKER_SCRIPT}} restart' then '{{DOCKER_SCRIPT}} logs --tail 50' (7) ssh docker ps --filter name={{CONTAINER_PREFIX}}, curl /api/health | jq, re-inspect revision (8) on success: keep pinned config, create a Linear ticket labelled bug + deployment-rollback, notify Slack; on failure: try older image, check environment, escalate (9) print rollback report (10) restore path: ssh sed -i rewriting the pinned tag regex back to ':latest', then /remote-deploy | MUTATES REMOTE STATE: edits {{COMPOSE_FILE}} in place on the remote host via sed -i; the only safety net is the timestamped cp backup in step 5 | canonical target of the deprecated /rollback-dev alias | failure modes: image not available (try older, manual pull, docker images | grep), services still failing (suspect environmental — DB/Redis/config), config restore fails (manual restore from backup, check SSH perms and disk) | PARITY GAP: Gemini omits step 10 (restore to latest) and the explicit sed -i command in step 5 — it says only 'Update docker-compose file to use specific image tag' | PARITY GAP: Gemini drops the bug / deployment-rollback label instruction and the whole Error Handling section | BRANCH DRIFT: Claude uses git log origin/{{MAIN_BRANCH}}; Gemini hardcodes origin/main

concepts.title: /remote-status

no marker in source either way | DOC DRIFT (both sides named): .claude/commands/README.md lists /rollback-dev in its 'Deprecated Aliases' table, described there as 'thin wrappers pointing to canonical /remote-* commands' and mapped to /remote-rollback; rollback-dev.md itself carries no DEPRECATED banner and is a full 272-line executable procedure, making it the only one of the five listed aliases that is not a wrapper — and its own restore step points at /remote-deploy, never at /remote-rollback

concepts.title: /search-pattern

concepts.title: /start-work

CONTRIBUTING.md is the northstar for conventions' — both must be followed | example given: /start-work 347 resolves to {{TICKET_PREFIX}}-347 | BRANCH DRIFT: Claude branches from dev (git checkout dev && git pull origin dev); Gemini toml branches from main (git checkout main && git pull origin main) | PARITY GAP: Gemini has no Linear MCP — step 1 degrades to 'verify ticket exists in Linear (use web UI or CLI)' | PARITY GAP: Gemini adds an Execute Commands block running !{git status} and !{git branch --show-current} that has no Claude equivalent, and it never issues the checkout/pull/branch commands itself | the stop-the-line gate text is preserved verbatim in both providers

concepts.title: /sync-linear
concepts.description: Derives ticket status from branch commits and writes status, labels and a progress comment back to the Linear ticket.
concepts.notes: invoked as /sync-linear (Claude) or /workflow:sync-linear (Gemini) | no args | Claude frontmatter allowed-tools includes wildcard mcp__{{MCP_LINEAR_SERVER}}__* | 8 ordered steps: (1) git branch --show-current | grep -oE '{{TICKET_PREFIX}}-[0-9]+' then mcp__{{MCP_LINEAR_SERVER}}__get_issue (2) git log origin/dev..HEAD --oneline and git diff origin/dev --stat (3) map work state to one of five ticket statuses (4) mcp__{{MCP_LINEAR_SERVER}}__update_issue for status, progress percentage, labels (5) mcp__{{MCP_LINEAR_SERVER}}__create_comment with the Progress Update template (6) link PR / related tickets / docs (7) apply labels in-progress, blocked, needs-review, needs-testing (8) tag stakeholders if the transition is significant | WRITE COMMAND: mutates Linear state — status, labels and comments — with no confirmation step in the source | five status mappings: commits but incomplete -> In Progress; complete without PR -> Ready for Review or stay In Progress; PR created -> In Review; PR merged -> Done (noted as often auto-synced by the GitHub-Linear integration for tickets named in commit messages, child stories closed manually); blocked -> Blocked | five documented scenarios with exact status transitions: Todo->In Progress, In Progress (no change), In Progress->Ready for Review, In Progress->Blocked, Ready for Review->In Review | sync cadence: daily during active work, before standup, after major progress, immediately when blocked, on PR create/merge | asserts Linear is the single source of truth for project status | BRANCH DRIFT: Claude diffs against origin/dev; Gemini toml diffs against origin/main | PARITY GAP: Gemini has no MCP calls at all — steps 4 and 5 degrade to 'Use Linear web UI or CLI', so on Gemini this command is advisory and writes nothing | PARITY GAP: Gemini greps the branch with the generic '[A-Z]+-[0-9]+' instead of the {{TICKET_PREFIX}} placeholder, and drops step 7 (labels) and step 8 (notify stakeholders)

concepts.title: /test-pr-docker

concepts.notes: institutional knowledge, no single source file | TWO SEPARATE MECHANISMS UNDER ONE NAME | (1) STOP-THE-LINE GATE: precondition on implementation agents (BE/FE/DE) — check the Linear ticket has AC/DoD; YES -> proceed, NO -> FULL STOP, route back to BSA/POPM; explicit clause 'You are NOT responsible for inventing AC/DoD'; gate owner listed as 'Implementer', blocking = YES | (2) STOP-THE-LINE AUTHORITY: every member human or AI may halt progress; sourced to Toyota's Andon cord | authority covers exactly 5 categories: architectural integrity, security concerns, maintainability issues, performance implications, scalability concerns | exercising it requires 4 steps: explain the concern with specifics, propose at least one alternative, document via ADR or #PATH_DECISION tag, post a comment on the Linear ticket | gate table lists 5 gates total: Stop-the-Line (Implementer), QAS Gate (QAS), Stage 1 Review (System Architect), Stage 2 Review (ARCHitect-CLI), HITL Merge ({{AUTHOR_NAME}}) — all marked blocking YES | enforcement is prompt-level only: .claude/commands/start-work.md carries the gate text; no hook, script, or CI check verifies AC/DoD exists | routing when AC/DoD is missing: @bsa

concepts.title: PR Validation Workflow (pr-validation.yml)
concepts.description: Checks PR rebase status, commit message format, PR title and Linear ticket reference.
concepts.notes: name PR Validation | trigger pull_request types [opened, synchronize, reopened, edited] | single job validate-pr on ubuntu-latest | checkout@v4 with fetch-depth 0 | four run steps | step 1 rebase check: git fetch origin base_ref, compares rev-parse origin/<base> to merge-base HEAD origin/<base>, emits ::error:: and exit 1 on mismatch — THIS IS THE ONLY HARD GATE in the file | step 2 commit message check: git log --format=%s base..HEAD piped into a while-read subshell, grep -qE for conventional-commit + [{{TICKET_PREFIX}}-N], allowlists ^Merge and ^🤖 Generated, emits ::warning:: only — never exits nonzero; also the loop runs in a pipeline subshell so no status could escape it anyway | step 3 PR title check: ::warning:: only | step 4 Linear ticket reference in PR body via env PR_BODY: ::warning:: only | GATES: rebase only; commit format, PR title and ticket reference are advisory and cannot fail the run | config KEY NAME only: TICKET_PREFIX (unsubstituted placeholder — until substituted the regexes match the literal string {{TICKET_PREFIX}}, so every real commit warns) | DOC DRIFT: docs/ci-cd/CI-CD-Pipeline-Guide.md Stage 1 says branch-name and PR-title violations 'block PR progression'; the implementation only warns, and there is no branch-name check at all in this workflow

concepts.notes: takes no arguments; exits 0 with 'No dark factory sessions running.' when tmux list-sessions has no ^factory- match | per session prints creation time via date -d @<epoch>, falling back to date -r <epoch>, then 'unknown' | per pane reads pane_index, pane_title, pane_pid, pane_current_command, pane_last_activity | liveness test is pgrep -P <pane_pid> -f claude — it only sees claude as a DIRECT child of the pane shell, so a claude wrapped in another process reads as dead | classification: no claude child = dead (red); claude present and now-pane_last_activity > 300 = idle (yellow); otherwise active (green); the 300-second threshold is hardcoded | aggregate line counts claude processes with pgrep -f claude, which matches any command line containing the substring 'claude' including this script's own greps | RSS total comes from 'ps -C claude -o rss=' summed by awk; -C is a procps/Linux flag that BSD/macOS ps does not support, so on macOS the sum is empty and the dashboard reports ~0MB while still claiming processes exist | no exit code other than 0; it is read-only and never touches tmux state | intended to be wrapped in 'watch -n 5' per README.md

concepts.title: factory-stop.sh
concepts.description: Interrupts agent panes, kills the session, removes worktrees, and archives per-agent logs.
concepts.notes: usage: factory-stop.sh [session-name]; with no argument it lists sessions matching ^factory- and read -rp prompts, but dies when stdin is not a tty | dies if tmux has-session fails for the named session | sources $HOME/.dark-factory/env if present for FACTORY_LOG_DIR, FACTORY_USE_WORKTREES, FACTORY_WORKTREE_DIR | shutdown: collects pane_id list, tmux send-keys C-c to every pane, then polls once per second for up to 30 seconds using pgrep -P <pane_pid> -f claude to decide whether any agent is still alive | worktree cleanup only when FACTORY_USE_WORKTREES is true: git worktree remove <dir> --force for each agent-* dir, then rmdir the session dir, every failure swallowed with || true | log archive: mv <FACTORY_LOG_DIR>/<session> to <FACTORY_LOG_DIR>/archive/<session>; mv is unguarded, so an existing archive entry for the same session name nests rather than replaces | DOC DRIFT: step 4 is commented 'Kill remaining panes' and the timeout branch prints 'Force-killing remaining panes', but the code only re-sends C-c and sleeps 1; the actual kill is tmux kill-session in step 5 | never SIGKILLs a hung claude process, so an agent ignoring SIGINT is terminated only as a side effect of the session dying

concepts.title: Feature Team Layout
concepts.description: Five-pane tmux layout starting TDM lead plus BE, FE, QAS, and RTE agents.
concepts.notes: sourced by factory-start.sh; requires SESSION_NAME and agent_workdir | 4 splits on top of the initial pane give 5 panes | the splits assign titles once, then a second re-title pass overwrites them because indices shift during splitting; the final mapping is 1 TDM (lead), 2 BE Developer, 3 QAS, 4 FE Developer, 5 RTE | DOC DRIFT: the ASCII layout comment at the top of the file shows row 2 as BE|FE and row 3 as QAS|RTE, but the final re-title pass puts QAS at index 3 and FE at index 4, so pane titles and the documented grid disagree | CLAUDE_FLAGS is '--dangerously-skip-permissions' only when FACTORY_AUTO_PERMISSIONS is true | only pane 1 receives a -p prompt (TDM lead, PRs via gh pr create, enqueue via gh pr merge --auto --squash, never merge directly); panes 2-5 launch bare claude sessions | ends by selecting pane 1 | matches the feature pane_count=5 branch in factory-start.sh

concepts.title: Merge Queue Policy
concepts.description: The single-path-to-trunk policy: GitHub merge queue with squash, enforced by ruleset not by client flags.
concepts.notes: 227 lines | states one allowed merge command: gh pr merge --auto --squash; all three team layouts embed exactly that string in the TDM prompt | explicitly denies that '--merge-queue' is a real gh option and states enforcement lives in GitHub branch rulesets, not client-side flags | prescribed ruleset: merge queue required on the main branch, merge method squash, max entries 5, 30-minute check timeout, ALLGREEN strategy, strict_required_status_checks_policy false, no bypass actors | ships dark-factory/templates/github/merge-queue-ruleset.json for import via Settings > Rules > Rulesets, with manual UI steps as a fallback | requires CI workflows to carry the merge_group event trigger; factory-setup.sh greps .github/workflows/*.yml for 'merge_group' as half its readiness gate | stop-the-line rule: if the queue is unavailable agents stop creating PRs, the TDM reports the blocker, and there is no fallback to direct merge | squash means the PR title becomes the trunk commit message, so PR titles must match 'type(scope): description [<PREFIX>-XXX]' | monitoring commands: gh pr checks, gh pr list --json number,title,mergeStateStatus, gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/mergequeue | uses {{MAIN_BRANCH}} and {{TICKET_PREFIX}} tokens

concepts.title: Knowledge Vault Subsystem
concepts.description: OKF v0.1 vault tooling: a zero-dependency structural validator, gate tests, starter bundle, and build prompts.
concepts.notes: core executable is knowledge-vault/scripts/validate-vault.mjs, 461 lines, node: builtins only, zero npm dependencies | it locates a vault by finding a directory containing _meta/vault-config.json (or --vault <dir>), reads that config, then walks every .md, .canvas and .base file | flags: --vault <dir>, --allow-broken-links (downgrades broken bundle links and missing manifest files to warnings), --strict-orphans (promotes the no-inbound-links warning to an error), --quiet | exits 1 when errors.length is non-zero, 0 otherwise; always prints a one-line summary of concepts, md files, canvases, errors and warnings | enforced gates: frontmatter required-field contract; description length against max_description_length; timestamp matching ^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$; status against the statuses list; domain against the domains list; every tag against the controlled tags vocabulary; resource presence for any type with resource_required; exact H2 section sequence equality against the type's sections array plus exactly one H1; existence on disk of every value in path_fields (resource, sources, docs); okf_version only in the root index.md and only matching the config's value | link discipline: wikilinks forbidden, leading-slash links are errors, repo-host blob/tree/raw URLs are errors, links escaping the repository are errors, and out-of-bundle links outside the '## Citations' H2 are errors except in index files and type 'guide' | any type marked stub:true must carry at least one out-of-bundle or external citation under Citations or it errors | reserved files: log.md must have no frontmatter, must have an H1, and warns without dated '## YYYY-MM-DD' entries; non-root index.md must have no frontmatter | manifest sync against _meta/manifest.json is bidirectional: a manifest id with no file is an error (warning under --allow-broken-links) but a file absent from the manifest is ALWAYS an error, because the manifest is the id allowlist against invented links | max_concept_lines is advisory only and is skipped for free-form types with zero declared sections, such as guide | canvas nodes of type file are resolved against the obsidian vault dir, the bundle, then the repo root, and error if none exists | knowledge-vault/tests/test-validator-gates.sh proves the gates bite: 2 assert_clean cases (the shipped starter bundle, and the bundle after the documented copy-and-rewrite) and 7 assert_error cases covering wikilink, repo-host URL, missing resource path, stub without citation, dangling canvas node, concept missing from the manifest, and a renamed section | knowledge-vault/templates/github/validate-vault.yml is an OPT-IN CI template with {{VAULT_DIR}} and {{MAIN_BRANCH}} tokens, pinning actions/setup-node@v4 at node-version 20 with no install step, and its own header warns that in the origin project the validator 'was wired into no workflow at all' | DOC DRIFT: that warning applies to this repo right now — grep over .github/workflows and package.json finds no reference to validate-vault.mjs or knowledge-vault, so the validator is run by nothing in CI here | this repo's own live vault config is docs/knowledge-vault/_meta/vault-config.json declaring bundle_root docs/knowledge-vault, okf_version 0.1, 5 domains, 4 statuses, 21 tags and 20 types | UNKNOWN: whether docs/knowledge-vault currently contains any concept files or a _meta/manifest.json — only vault-config.json and this build's manifest-parts were observed

concepts.title: Harness Sync Engine
concepts.description: 3366-line bash engine that pulls upstream harness domains via GitHub tarball while preserving fork renames, substitutions, and protected files.
concepts.notes: scripts/sync-claude-harness.sh, 3366 lines, 57 functions, set -e | 10 commands dispatched by case on $1: init|status|version|diff|sync|manifest|rollback|conflicts|releases|help | check_dependencies + migrate_metadata_to_root run for every command except help | hard deps: curl, node, python3 (python3 only for YAML->JSON via PyYAML; missing python3 or PyYAML => print_warning + HAS_MANIFEST=false, silent degrade to legacy) | metadata at repo root (v2.10.0+): .harness-sync.json, .harness-backup/, .harness-patches/, .harness-manifest.yml, .harness-manifest.schema.json; legacy .claude/ copies auto-copied forward by migrate_metadata_to_root and left in place | .sync-exclude and .sync-exclude.default stay under .claude/ (legacy fallback only) | tmp workspace /tmp/claude-harness-sync-$$, rm -rf on EXIT trap | fetch_upstream: curl -sL https://api.github.com/repos/$UPSTREAM_REPO/tarball/$ref piped to tar xz --strip-components=1; ABORTS if $TMP_DIR/.claude absent even when sync_scope excludes .claude | get_upstream_sha / get_latest_release / list_releases hit api.github.com unauthenticated | do_sync pipeline per domain: apply_all_substitutions(DOMAIN_TMP) -> build sync_plan (is_excluded -> resolve_rename -> compare_file_with_paths) -> run_preflight -> create_backup -> cp substituted TMP file over local | substitution happens in TMP_DIR BEFORE preflight so the token scanner sees post-substitution state | create_backup writes .harness-backup/<domain>/<SYNC_TIMESTAMP>/, prunes to last 3 timestamps per domain; SYNC_TIMESTAMP shared across all domains in one run so do_rollback can restore every domain from one timestamp | do_rollback picks newest timestamp via date -d (GNU-only flag; returns 0 epoch on BSD date) and copies back into $PROJECT_ROOT/<domain>/ | update_sync_metadata writes BOTH key families: last_synced_commit/last_synced_version/last_synced_at AND last_sync_commit/last_sync_version/last_sync_timestamp, plus sync_history capped at 10 | flags: --dry-run --version <tag> --latest --scope <csv> --no-placeholders --skip-preflight --generate-patches; unknown args silently shifted, never error | no manifest + no --dry-run => print_error + return 1; with --dry-run => warns and previews with legacy .claude-only scope | REQUIRES BASH 4: do_diff line 1560 'declare -A dir_rename_counts' + line 1702 ${!arr[@]}; on macOS /bin/bash 3.2 do_diff dies with 'declare: -A: invalid option' and produces no output - this is the single root cause of 12/50 failures in tests/test-rename-diff.sh, 6/54 in tests/test-protected-files.sh, and 7 failures in tests/test-fork-sync.sh | DOC DRIFT: manifest sync.conflict_strategy (upstream-wins|local-wins|prompt|three-way) is only READ for display in do_status line 2453; no branch anywhere implements it - do_sync unconditionally cp's upstream over local (de-facto upstream-wins) and the conflicts counter passed to update_sync_metadata is hardcoded 0 | DOC DRIFT: manifest sync.auto_substitute documented as 'Set to false to sync raw upstream files' is never read; only --no-placeholders suppresses substitution | DOC DRIFT: manifest sync.substitution_extensions is never read; apply_all_substitutions hardcodes .md .json .yml .yaml .sh .py .txt .toml .ts .mjs .bib .cff (.bib/.cff extra vs the manifest list) | DOC DRIFT: manifest 'replaced' section documented to skip files and log 'Skipped (replaced): <path>' - that string does not exist in the script; get_protected_patterns reads only data.protected, so 'replaced' entries are counted in status/validate output and otherwise OVERWRITTEN | DOC DRIFT: show_help says both 'sync requires a manifest ... sync will fail' and 'Without a manifest, the script uses legacy file-level copy behavior' | is_protected falls back to substring match after glob match, so a short protected pattern silently protects unrelated paths | do_conflicts only scans $CLAUDE_DIR for *.conflict, ignoring other sync domains | UNKNOWN: is any *.conflict file ever written? no writer for that suffix found in the script

concepts.title: Harness Manifest Schema
concepts.description: JSON Schema plus template YAML declaring how a downstream fork customizes the harness: identity, substitutions, renames, protected, replaced, sync prefs.
concepts.notes: schema draft 2020-12, additionalProperties:false at root, required [manifest_version, identity] | 7 top-level sections: manifest_version, identity, substitutions, renames, protected, replaced, sync | repo's own .harness-manifest.yml is manifest_version 1.1 with 27 identity keys all still {{PLACEHOLDER}} values, empty substitutions/renames/protected/replaced, sync_scope listing all 6 allowed domains | schema required identity subset: PROJECT_NAME PROJECT_REPO PROJECT_SHORT GITHUB_ORG TICKET_PREFIX MAIN_BRANCH (6 of 27) | identity key names mirror scripts/setup-template.sh {{...}} tokens exactly | v1.0 = paths relative to .claude/, v1.1+ = repo-root-relative; do_sync sets USE_ROOT_PATHS=true when manifest_version is 1.1 or lexically greater and prefixes $CURRENT_DOMAIN/ onto every manifest lookup key | renames: trailing / marks a directory rename; resolve_rename checks exact file match first, then directory prefix match, then passthrough (file wins over directory) | ENFORCEMENT GAP vs schema: validate_manifest is hand-rolled bash+node, NOT a JSON Schema validator - it checks only manifest_version regex ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$, presence of identity plus the 6 required subkeys, and emits WARNINGS (never errors) for absolute or .. rename paths; concepts.title: Multi-Domain Sync Scope Resolution
concepts.description: How the sync engine resolves which harness directories to sync, from manifest sync_scope, a --scope override, or the .claude default.
concepts.notes: resolution order: get_sync_scope() reads manifest -> optional --scope <csv> override replaces it wholesale -> empty result falls back to SYNC_SCOPE=(.claude) | get_sync_scope does NOT use the parsed manifest JSON; it re-reads the raw YAML line-by-line with grep/sed looking for '^\s*sync_scope:' then consuming following '-' lines, stripping quotes and trailing slash - so a sync_scope in JSON-style flow syntax or unusual indentation is silently missed and the default applies | 6 ALLOWED_DOMAINS hardcoded at line 57: .claude .gemini .codex .cursor .agents dark-factory; anything else prints '[WARN] Ignoring unknown sync domain: X' and is dropped, not an error | --scope validates against the same allowlist; if every entry is invalid it is the ONE scope path that hard-fails (print_error + return 1); --scope never rewrites .harness-manifest.yml | domains are processed sequentially in a for loop; a domain is SKIPPED with a warning when absent from the fetched upstream tarball OR absent locally (v2.10.0 does not auto-create local domain dirs) | preflight failure inside the loop does `continue` - it skips only that domain and the sync proceeds to the next one; the process still exits 0 | per-domain state carried by globals DOMAIN_DIR / DOMAIN_TMP / CURRENT_DOMAIN, consumed by compare_file_with_paths, generate_patch, run_preflight and create_backup | SYNC_TIMESTAMP is reset once per do_sync and shared by every domain backup so rollback restores the whole set together | patches dir is created once outside the loop; APPLY_ORDER.md is generated after the loop so entries from all domains accumulate | release domains (docs/, scripts/, patterns_library/) are explicitly not in the allowlist | DOC DRIFT: fetch_upstream hard-errors 'No .claude directory found in upstream repository' regardless of sync_scope, so a fork scoped to only .gemini/ still cannot sync if upstream lacks .claude | DOC DRIFT: run_preflight's scope-violation error string is hardcoded 'files outside .claude/ would be modified' even in multi-domain runs
